newsitem.title: MALI: New Malian opposition alliance forms.
newsitem.headline: New Malian opposition alliance forms.

text.p: Six political parties in Mali formed a new left-of-centre opposition alliance on Sunday to contest national elections planned for later this year.
A statement from the Front for Change and Democracy (FCD) accused supporters of President Alpha Oumar Konare of killing democratic debate.
It criticised International Monetary Fund and World Bank-sponsored reforms, saying the people were suffering and state industry was being sold off for a quick profit.
No date has been set for presidential and parliamentary elections which must be held by June.

The elections are likely to pit the new coalition against Konare's supporters in the Alliance for Democracy in Mali ADEMA and the eight-party Rally of Patriotic Forces (RFP), which is to the right of ADEMA.
Mariam Travele, widow of Mali's independence president Modibo Keita, chaired the first meeting of the new alliance.
Mali's 1992 election followed the 1991 overthrow of dictator Moussa Traore by soldiers who subsequently stepped down and has been hailed as a democratic success by friends such as the United States.
Konare, a historian, is expected to seek a further five-year term.
